reviewer_notes: HUMAN-MAINTAINED. This file is the ONLY place the meaning of a scope token is declared. Nothing infers a relationship from spelling, naming similarity, or folder location.

A token that is not registered here is UNKNOWN, and an UNKNOWN token fails closed: any scope comparison touching it returns SCOPE_UNKNOWN_OVERLAP and goes to human review. That is deliberate. The cost of a review item is small; the cost of silently deciding two masters do not collide is a wrong logo shipping to a market.

DISJOINT is never inferred from the mere absence of an edge. Two registered tokens are disjoint ONLY where this file says so — via mutually_exclusive_children, mutually_exclusive_roots on a closed_world axis, or an explicit disjoint_peers entry.

Adding a token, an alias, or an edge CHANGES how existing approvals would be read. That is why every decision pins taxonomy_version. Bump the version on any semantic change and expect TAXONOMY_REVIEW_REQUIRED on affected decisions.

The token sets below are seeded from what DIP-0A/0C actually observed plus the examples the business gave. They are deliberately small: a short honest registry beats a long speculative one, because every unregistered token fails safely.

v1.1.0 (DIP-0C3d) adds the MEDIA axis. Media answers 'where may this be used' and is INDEPENDENT of products, which answers 'what is being designed'. A palette approved for DIGITAL is not approved for the press, and encoding that inside the product tree would collapse two questions into one. SCREEN is deliberately NOT declared a parent of WEB or SOCIAL_MEDIA: the business has not said it is, so those comparisons return SCOPE_UNKNOWN_OVERLAP and go to review rather than being guessed from naming similarity.

markets.notes: Closed-world: BBROSE sells into a known set of markets. Distinct roots (EU / US / CN / GLOBAL_OTHER) are mutually exclusive by declaration, so EU vs US is DISJOINT. EU is a PARENT of its member states, so EU vs FR OVERLAPS.

UK.notes: Deliberately NOT a child of EU.

products.notes: A hierarchy: COSMETICS > MAKEUP > {LIP_GLOSS, MASCARA, ...}. An ancestor OVERLAPS its descendants. Siblings under a parent declared mutually_exclusive_children are DISJOINT.

PACKAGING.notes: A GENERAL token: it cuts across the product tree rather than sitting inside it. It is never disjoint from anything by structure alone — comparisons against it are UNKNOWN unless an explicit edge says otherwise.

lockups.notes: PRIMARY is a GENERAL/parent scope: it OVERLAPS PRIMARY_HORIZONTAL and PRIMARY_VERTICAL. The two orientations are disjoint ONLY because mutually_exclusive_children says so explicitly — orientation is not self-evidently a partition of brand usage. mutually_exclusive_roots is FALSE here: PRIMARY vs STACKED is NOT assumed disjoint, because a stacked lockup may well be a primary one. Those comparisons return UNKNOWN and go to review, which is the honest answer.

variant_roles.notes: The role a file plays relative to the canonical master. MASTER is the canonical role; the others are subordinate and can never become the master by reclassification alone.

media.notes: Where or how an asset may be used. mutually_exclusive_roots is FALSE: media tokens are NOT assumed to partition the world, so two registered tokens with no declared relationship return SCOPE_UNKNOWN_OVERLAP and go to review. SCREEN vs WEB is UNKNOWN — a web page is shown on a screen, and until the business SAYS whether WEB sits under SCREEN, guessing either way would be exactly the inference this taxonomy forbids. PRINT and DIGITAL are disjoint only because disjoint_peers declares it, and PACKAGING_PRINT inherits that disjointness from its parent PRINT.
